From German Bambi, from Italian bambino (“child”), after the fictional character Bambi created by the Austrian author Felix Salten (1869–1945).

parole.significato: A four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with collapsible half-hood, two double seats facing each other, and an outside seat…
parole.testo: From dialectal German Barutsche, from Italian baroccio, from Late Latin *birotium, from Latin birotus (“chariot”), from bi- (“two”) + rota (“wheel”). The spelling was altered in English as if the word had come from French. Doublet of britchka.
Borrowed from German Kartaune, from Italian quartana (“25-pounder cannon”).

parole.significato: A piece of instrumental music of the eighteenth century similar to the serenade, and often performed outdoors.
parole.testo: From German Kassation, from Italian cassazione

parole.significato: A transfer of funds between different account holders, carried out by the bank according to payer's written instruction…
parole.testo: Via German, from Italian giro (“circulation”), from Latin gyrus (“circle”), from Ancient Greek γῦρος (gûros, “circle”), from Proto-Indo-European *gew- (“to curve, to bend”).

parole.significato: Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes, a variety of the cabbage, having a turnip-shaped edible stem.
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Kohlrabi, from Kohl (“cabbage”) + Italian rape (“turnips”), from cavoli rape, the plural of cavolo rapa (“cole rape”).

parole.significato: A confection made from a paste of almonds, sugar and egg white as a binder.
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Marzipan, from Italian marzapane, Venetan marzapane. parole.significato: A full score, conductor's score (with a separate line for every part).
parole.testo: From German Partitur, from Italian partitura (“partition, musical score”) , from Latin partito, from partīre (“divide, partition, share”) (Classical Latin partīrī) and -ura.

parole.significato: An alto, tenor, or bass instrument of the shawm family.
parole.testo: From German Pommer, from Middle High German bumhart, from Italian bombarda.

parole.significato: A form of rusk, usually sweetened bread enriched with eggs that is baked and then sliced and toasted until dry and cris…
parole.testo: From German Zwieback, from zwie- (“twi-, two-”) + backen (“to bake”) (i.e. “twice-baked”), a calque of Italian biscotto (but not to be confused with it).
